news.headline: Govt unveils new plan to fast track $6 billion refinery upgrade projects
news.summary: Petroleum Division submitted amendments to the Brownfield Refining Policy 2023 to the Cabinet Committee on Energy: refineries (PARCO, Attock Refinery/ARL, Pakistan Refinery/PRL, National Refinery/NRL, Cnergyico) that sign OGRA Upgrade Agreements within 90 days get a seven-year package - minimum 10% customs/regulatory duty maintained on imported gasoline and diesel for seven years, a 10% deemed duty incentive on locally produced gasoline/diesel, and sales tax exemption on imported plant, machinery, equipment and materials - to unlock nearly $6 billion in upgrades.

news.headline: PSX Closing Bell: Falls Off A Cliff
news.summary: Monday final close: KSE-100 ended at 179,927.04, down 2,314.73 points (-1.27%) from previous close of 182,241.77; KSE-100 volume 365.01m shares, All-Share Index volume 845.28m shares, market value traded Rs35.55bn; breadth 13 advancers vs 87 decliners of 100 index companies; top gainers GHNI +5.60%, CNERGY +3.72%, GHGL +1.97%, ATRL +1.93%, RMPL +0.69%; top losers TGL -4.03%, HGFA -3.38%, DGKC -3.20%, MLCF -3.17%, POWER -2.99%; report attributes the drop to the surge in international oil prices and heightened geopolitical uncertainty (US-Iran Strait of Hormuz), prompting broad-based selling in banking, cement, fertilizer and energy stocks.

news.headline: PKR strengthens again, hits 195-day winning run vs USD
news.summary: Rupee added 3.08 paisa in Monday's interbank session to settle at Rs278.02/USD (from Friday's close of Rs278.05), extending a 195-consecutive-day winning streak vs the dollar (cumulative +Rs3.4018, +1.22% over the streak); intraday band Rs278.20-278.00; open market Rs278.80 buy / Rs279.10 sell.

news.headline: Pakistan car sales jump 39% in FY26
news.summary: FY26 cumulative car/LCV/van/jeep sales reached 206,436 units, +39.4% YoY vs FY25's 148,042; June 2026 sales 22,741 units (+4.4% YoY, +28.8% MoM), though passenger cars alone fell 12.9% YoY in June (15,378 units) while LCVs/vans/jeeps rose 79.0% YoY (7,363 units); June brand figures cited: Suzuki 7,719 units (Alto 7,239, Every 480, Cultus 439, Swift 1,668), Toyota 2,650 units, Honda 2,594 units, Hyundai 288 units - no PSX-ticker-level breakdown given in the article.

news.headline: Sazgar produces 2,488 three-wheelers, 2,374 four-wheelers in June 2026
news.summary: SAZEW June 2026 output: 2,488 three-wheelers produced (3,267 sold) and 2,374 four-wheelers produced (2,720 sold), combined 4,862 units produced vs 5,987 sold; vs May 2026, four-wheeler production +47.5% (sales +69.6%) and three-wheeler production +52.5% (sales +99.7%) - sales outpacing production indicates inventory drawdown.

news.headline: Nestle Pakistan board meeting notice posted
news.summary: PSX corporate announcements / DPS company page for NESTLE show a board meeting notice posted Jul 13, 2026; agenda/date of the meeting itself not specified in the source pages reviewed - routine notice, no dividend or results figure disclosed yet.

news.headline: PSX plunges over 2% intraday as US reimposes naval blockade on Iran
news.summary: Tuesday intraday, from previous close of 179,927.04/179,927.05 (Monday): Dawn reported KSE-100 at 176,462.15, down 3,464.89 points (-1.93%); Pakistan Observer reported it down 3,733.34 points to 176,193.70 (-2.07%); Business Recorder reported it shedding over 3,600 points in opening minutes to 176,309.50 as of 9:43am, down 3,617.54 points (-2.01%), with index-heavy MARI, OGDC, PPL, HUBCO, MCB, MEBL and UBL trading in the red across autos, cement, banks, E&P, OMCs and power sectors. Driver: President Trump announced the US is reinstating a naval blockade of Iranian shipping through the Strait of Hormuz effective Jul 14 (CENTCOM cited 4:00pm ET start), plus a 20% fee on cargo transiting the strait; Brent crude +$1.50 to $84.80/bbl (+1.8%), WTI +$1.70 to $79.84/bbl (+2.2%), four-week highs; AKD Securities' Awais Ashraf quoted: 'The decline is broad-based, with cyclical sectors witnessing the sharpest percentage losses amid heightened uncertainty.'

news.source: Business Recorder / Geo News / Dawn / Express Tribune

news.summary: Same Tuesday Strait-of-Hormuz story continued to deepen through the session (previous close 179,927.04): Business Recorder reported the index at 174,942.03 as of 12:04pm, down 4,985.01 points (-2.77%); Geo News reported an intraday low of 174,615.03, down 5,312.01 points (-2.95%), with an intraday high of 178,112.04 (-1,815 points, -1.01%); Dawn/Express Tribune reported 175,338.25 (-4,588.79 pts) at 12:30pm and 175,683.38 (-4,243.66 pts, -2.36%) at 12:44pm; across-the-board selling continued in autos, cement, banks, E&P, OMCs and power, with MARI, OGDC, PPL, HUBCO, MCB, MEBL and UBL still trading in the red; no confirmed final closing-bell figure found in the sources reviewed as of this cycle.

news.summary: Continuation of the same Tuesday Strait-of-Hormuz story (previous close 179,927.05): Investing.com's Karachi 100 quote page, timestamped 06:05:45 and marked 'Delayed Data', showed the index last at 173,840.94, down 6,086.12 points (-3.38%), with the day's low at 173,785.30 and day's open at 178,053.66 - a deeper decline than the 174,615.03 low and 175,683.38 (-2.36%) level reported by Business Recorder/Geo News/Dawn/Express Tribune earlier in the same session (logged in the prior newslog entry). news.headline: Select Technologies raises Rs3.02bn through IPO, becomes 1st PSX listing of new fiscal year
news.summary: Select Technologies Limited, a Pakistani smartphone and consumer-appliances maker, raised Rs3.02bn via IPO of 88.9m ordinary shares (10% of post-issue paid-up capital); floor price Rs28.00/share, strike price discovered at Rs34.00/share (21% premium over floor) after book-building; issue oversubscribed 3.23x with ~13,000 investors participating (banks, mutual funds, insurers, pension funds, brokerages, HNWIs, retail). Not currently a KSE100/KMI30 universe constituent - logged for macro/primary-market sentiment context only; ticker symbol not confirmed in source reviewed.

news.headline: Dada Partners advises Nishat Group on Pakistan's largest private cross-border listed-company acquisition (Rafhan Maize)
news.summary: Nishat Group acquired 73.9% of Rafhan Maize Products Company Limited (RMPL) for approximately PKR 66 billion - 51% bought from majority shareholder Ingredion Incorporated (USA, which retains a strategic minority stake), 20.5% from a minority shareholder, and 2.4% via mandatory public offer - taking Nishat Group's total stake to a super-majority 75.9%; described in the article as the largest private-sector cross-border M&A of a listed Pakistani company, excluding privatizations. Dada Partners (Private) Limited was exclusive financial advisor to Nishat Group; Cornelius, Lane and Mufti (CLM) was legal counsel; Next Capital was Manager to the Offer.

news.headline: Hormuz tensions wipe out over 6,400 points at PSX - KSE-100 confirmed close
news.summary: Tuesday final close confirmed: Express Tribune reported KSE-100 'closed at 173,518.82, down 6,408.23 points, or 3.56%, from the previous close of 179,927.05, as selling intensified throughout the session'; volume 912.6m shares, value Rs45.6bn traded, 498 companies traded (40 up, 439 down, 19 unchanged); major decliners named: UBL, Engro Holdings, Fauji Fertiliser, Lucky Cement, Meezan Bank, OGDC, HBL, PPL and MCB Bank. Corroborating Dawn report (timestamped 3:00pm PKT) had the index at 173,839.01, down 6,088.03 points (-3.38%), quoting AKD Securities director of research Awais Ashraf: 'The decline is broad-based, with cyclical sectors witnessing the sharpest percentage losses amid heightened uncertainty over the medium-term outlook due to the emerging geopolitical situation.' Same Strait-of-Hormuz naval-blockade driver as prior entries this cycle; this is the deepest and now-final read of Tuesday's session, superseding the earlier intraday/delayed-quote entries logged above.

news.headline: Pakistan retires record Rs4.7tr debt ahead of maturity
news.summary: Pakistan retired Rs4.7 trillion (approx. $17bn) of public debt ahead of maturity - described as the largest early-retirement liability-management exercise in the country's history; composition 51% owed to SBP, 49% market debt/government securities; Adviser to the Finance Minister Khurram Schehzad called it the 'largest and most sustained liability management operation,' with average maturity of public debt extended from 2.7 years (FY24) to 3.8 years (FY26) - supportive for macro stability and refinancing risk, no direct PSX-ticker impact disclosed.
